quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What following distance should you normally keep from the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you. Increase this distance if conditions are bad.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that run parallel to the road?

options.text: Avoid crossing the tracks at all.

questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or road seams at an angle of at least 45 degrees. Make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing slowly can catch your tires and throw off your balance.

questions.question: What should you do to swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to go. To go left, press the left handgrip then the right to recover. To go right, press the right handgrip then the left.

questions.question: Is the oily strip in the center of a lane safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe unless the road is wet.
Usually safe unless it is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in the center of traffic lanes. This area is safe for motorcycles unless the road is wet. The oily strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride around it while staying in the lane.

questions.question: Which is NOT a common cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to get out of a wobble.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when being passed from behind?

options.text: Use the left portion of the lane.
Use the center portion of the lane.
Use the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of the lane is safest. Riding near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding far from it may make the driver return to your lane unsafely.

questions.question: What does swerving on a motorcycle require?

options.text: You should swerve on slippery roads to avoid hazards.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs a lot of traction to work safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.explanation: Two seconds is usually enough, but increase your distance when conditions need longer stopping time, such as bad weather, at night, when you cannot see ahead, or during heavy traffic.

questions.question: What kind of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit and other regulation signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths: the left, center, and right portions of the lane.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely, have no scratches, resist penetration, allow clear side views, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you want to turn.
Do not drag your feet on the road.
Do not look at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not look at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet on the road because they could catch and make you lose control. Always watch for other traffic on the road.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they seem to be:

options.text: Going faster than they really are.
Going slower than they really are.
Not moving when they really are moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they really are.
questions.explanation: Because motorcycles are small, they may look like they are going faster than they actually are.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on to be more visible at intersections. Ride in a lane position where oncoming drivers can see you easily. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can react if needed. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: In crashes between a motorcycle and a car, what percentage are caused by the car driver not yielding the right-of-way to the motorcycle?
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: The center of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place for a motorcycle to ride.
Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
Often has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of each lane. On dry roads, this area is usually safe to ride on. Avoid large buildups of oil and grease, which are common at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To avoid fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of these, except:

options.text: Limit how far you ride each day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Ride no more than about six hours a day and take a break every two hours. Do not take artificial stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, you will have the most room to react if you are riding:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most room to recover if a wind blast from a passing vehicle affects your control.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel segment lengths based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan routes based on your least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to prevent fatigue. Put inexperienced riders behind experienced ones so they can be watched. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Try to speed up while braking.

questions.explanation: Release the brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. If you lock the rear brake on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real location and speed.

questions.question: What should you NOT tell a passenger to do before riding?

options.text: Get on after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between yourself and the rider.
Keep legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between yourself and the rider.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to board after the engine starts. They should sit forward close to you and hold the handholds or your waist. They must keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: When are you least likely to see a deer or moose?
questions.explanation: Deer and moose are most active in late evening, at night, and in early morning hours.
